summary: Created TestGetCountriesAPI test fixture (namespace TestDriver\API) that registers IDs and ISOs parameters individually via manageIDs().register() and manageISOs().register() — no OrRule, for isolated per-path testing.
Created TestGetCountriesBySetAPI test fixture (namespace TestDriver\API) that uses OrRule via manageAllParamsRule().register(), mirroring the existing TestGetCountryBySetAPI (singular) pattern.

Created AppCountriesAPITraitTest with 11 integration tests covering: no-params returns empty array, single/multiple ID resolution, single/multiple ISO resolution, invalid ID validation error (VALIDATION_COUNTRY_ID_NOT_EXISTS), invalid ISO validation error (VALIDATION_COUNTRY_ISO_NOT_EXISTS), ISO case insensitivity (uppercase DE resolves correctly), manual selectAppCountries(), OrRule rejects no-params, OrRule resolves from IDs, OrRule resolves from ISOs, OrRule rejects both IDs and ISOs simultaneously.

Fixed AppCountryIDsHandler and AppCountryISOsHandler resolveValueFromSubject() to return null (not empty array) when the parameter has no request value — this is required for the BaseParamsHandlerContainer 'first non-null wins' iteration to fall through to the next handler when registering both individually. Without this fix, the IDs handler would always return [] and the ISOs handler would never be reached.
Run composer dump-autoload — both new fixture classes registered in autoload_classmap.php. DB unavailable in this environment, but autoload classmap was regenerated (exit code 0).
PHP syntax check passed for all 5 created/modified files.

comments.note: AppCountryIDsHandler and AppCountryISOsHandler: the original resolveValueFromSubject() return type was array (not nullable), which caused the BaseParamsHandlerContainer 'first non-null wins' iteration to always stop at the IDs handler even when no IDs were provided. Fixed to return ?array and check getValue() !== null before calling getCountries(). This is a behaviour correction, not just a style fix.

tests/application/assets/classes/TestDriver/API/TestGetCountryBySetAPI.php uses namespace application\assets\classes\TestDriver\API — inconsistent with all other test fixture API classes which use TestDriver\API. The new TestGetCountriesBySetAPI.php correctly follows TestDriver\API. The old file should be migrated to TestDriver\API in a future cleanup WP.

AppCountriesRuleHandler::resolveValueFromSubject() still returns array() (not null) when no valid set is found. This is acceptable for the OrRule path (only one handler is registered, so there is no next handler to fall through to), but the inconsistency with the fixed ID/ISO handlers could cause confusion. A future improvement: return null when getCountries() returns an empty array to keep the pattern consistent.

Live PHPUnit execution blocked by MySQL unavailability in sandbox (same environment limitation as Developer). Incident recorded at project level.

comments.note: test_methodResolvesWithMultipleISOs() asserts count(2) but does not assert which specific country objects are returned (no assertSame for $countryDE/$countryFR at specific indices). The multiple-IDs counterpart does assert both objects and their order. Minor gap — not a failure, but worth noting for consistency.

When both countryIDs and countryISOs are provided in the individual-registration path (TestGetCountriesAPI), the IDs handler wins silently and the ISOs handler is never reached (correct by design — individual registration has no mutual exclusivity). This behaviour is untested but is architecturally correct and documented by the fixture's docblock.

No test covers the case where countryIDs is an empty string or whitespace-only value to confirm it resolves to null (triggering handler fall-through). IDListParameter and StringListParameter both filter empty-after-trim values and return null for empty results, but an explicit test would confirm the end-to-end fall-through.

comments.note: test_methodResolvesWithMultipleISOs() — added assertSame($countryDE, $resolved[0]) and assertSame($countryFR, $resolved[1]) after the existing assertCount(2). The multiple-IDs counterpart (test_methodResolvesWithMultipleIDs) already asserts both objects at specific indices; this brings the ISO test to parity. Non-behavioral change — does not affect what is being tested, only strengthens the assertion specificity.

test_setIsValidWithCountryISOs() — added assertSame($countryDE, $countries[0]) and assertSame($countryFR, $countries[1]) after the existing assertCount(2). The OrRule IDs counterpart (test_setIsValidWithCountryIDs) already asserts both objects and their order; this brings the OrRule ISOs test to parity. Non-behavioral change.

[documentation-forward] AppCountriesAPITrait docblock only mentions manageAppCountriesParams() in one line. The trait's usage section should be expanded to document the two distinct registration patterns: (1) individual IDs/ISOs registration via manageIDs()->register() + manageISOs()->register() for isolated per-path handling, and (2) OrRule registration via manageAllParamsRule()->register() for mutual exclusivity. These are the two primary consumer patterns and both should be illustrated in the docblock with a brief example or @see reference to TestGetCountriesAPI / TestGetCountriesBySetAPI respectively.

AppCountriesRuleHandler::resolveValueFromSubject() returns array (not null) when no valid set is found — noted as a pre-existing inconsistency with the fixed IDsHandler/ISOsHandler null-return pattern. Acceptable for the OrRule path (single handler registered, no fall-through needed), but worth standardising in a future cleanup WP for conceptual consistency across all handlers.

TestGetCountriesAPI.php — KEY_COUNTRY_IDS constant is used as the response key regardless of whether the value was resolved from IDs or ISOs. The constant name accurately describes the response shape (always country IDs), but could mislead maintainers into thinking it is only populated by the IDs handler. A comment on the constant clarifying 'response key for resolved country IDs, populated from either the IDs or ISOs path' would improve clarity.
